import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 613

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/613](https://www.erdosproblems.com/613)
-/

namespace Erdos613

/--
**Erdős Problem 613:**
Let $n \geq 3$ and $G$ be a graph with $\binom{2n+1}{2} - \binom{n}{2} - 1$ edges.
Must $G$ be the union of a bipartite graph and a graph with maximum degree less than $n$?
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_613 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∀ n ≥ 3, ∀ (V : Type*) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), [DecidableRel G.Adj] →
        G.edgeFinset.card = Nat.choose (2 * n + 1) 2 - Nat.choose n 2 - 1 →
        ∃ (B D : SimpleGraph V), [DecidableRel B.Adj] → [DecidableRel D.Adj] →
          G = B ⊔ D ∧ B.IsBipartite ∧ ∀ v, D.degree v < n := by
  sorry

end Erdos613

reformulations.difference: The statement inserts universal DecidableRel binders, including after the existential graph witnesses, and expresses the maximum-degree bound pointwise.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Classically every adjacency relation has a decidability instance, and DecidableRel is a subsingleton. Consequently these binders neither restrict the graphs nor make the existential conclusion vacuous; the finite edge and neighbour counts are instance-independent. For n ≥ 3, the pointwise condition ∀ v, D.degree v < n is equivalent to D.maxDegree < n, including the empty vertex type. Review613.full_query_iff in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean proves equivalence of the complete positive query with the direct classical formulation using unconditional graph witnesses and maxDegree, without using the sorry theorem.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/613 (including mathematical remarks and status; retrieved through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/613)

Oleg Pikhurko, “Size Ramsey Numbers of Stars Versus 3-chromatic Graphs,” Combinatorica 21 (2001), 403–412: publisher abstract at https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s004930100004 (full text was paywalled).
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the cited question. The source records Pikhurko’s disproof, already with a counterexample at n = 5, matching answer(False) and research solved. Lean checks verified that both natural-number subtractions agree with ordinary subtraction throughout n ≥ 3, that the edge threshold is positive, and that a concrete 17-edge graph at n = 3 satisfies the hypotheses and admits the required decomposition. Empty/singleton cases were checked. An additional Lean equivalence shows that any overlap between B and D can be removed without increasing degrees, so no edge-disjointness hypothesis is missing.
